framework_rationale: MEDDPICC fits SQM because this is an enterprise industrial purchase across 3 large 24/7 lithium sites in the Atacama, where operations (Rodrigo, Head of Operations), safety, IT/OT and procurement will all weigh in, and a partner/integrator in Chile is likely to shape delivery. The email gives strong Pain and partial Metrics (crew cost and hazard) but leaves the Economic Buyer, Decision Process and Paper Process open beyond a Q3 budget conversation, and MEDDPICC makes exactly those gaps explicit for the BDR's first emails. BANT would collapse this into budget/authority/need/timing and miss the buying committee, competition (status quo contracted crews) and procurement path; SPICED is tuned to recurring SaaS expansion rather than a new multi-site industrial deployment.

elements.name: Metrics
elements.evidence: Contracted crews are expensive and hazardous
elements.missing: Quantified current crew cost, inspection frequency, hours, incident rates and target coverage per site
elements.discovery_question: Roughly what do the contracted inspection crews cost you per site per year, and how often do they inspect today?

elements.name: Economic Buyer
elements.evidence: Internal budget conversation scheduled for Q3 (budget owner not named; contact is Head of Operations, Northern Operations Division)
elements.missing: Who owns and signs the budget for this initiative and whether Rodrigo holds it
elements.discovery_question: Who else will be part of the Q3 budget conversation, and who ultimately signs off on the spend?

elements.name: Decision Criteria
elements.missing: Technical requirements (desert heat/dust, connectivity, docks, BVLOS, integrations) and commercial criteria
elements.discovery_question: What would a drone platform need to prove to work reliably in your Atacama conditions?

elements.name: Decision Process
elements.evidence: Internal budget conversation scheduled for Q3
elements.missing: Evaluation steps, stakeholders, pilot expectations and decision date
elements.discovery_question: What steps would you expect between now and the Q3 budget discussion, for example a pilot at one site?

elements.name: Paper Process
elements.missing: Procurement, legal, IT/OT security review, vendor onboarding and contracting path at SQM
elements.discovery_question: How does SQM usually procure new technology like this: direct vendor contract, tender, or through a local integrator?

elements.name: Identify Pain
elements.evidence: Contracted crews are expensive and hazardous; 3 large-scale 24/7 sites need inspection
elements.missing: Business consequence in numbers and which assets/inspections are most painful
elements.discovery_question: Which inspections are the most hazardous or costly for the crews today?

elements.name: Champion
elements.evidence: Rodrigo Castillo, Head of Operations, reached out directly via flytbase.com/contact
elements.missing: Confirmation that Rodrigo will advocate internally and has influence over the budget decision
elements.discovery_question: Would you be open to us helping you build the case for the Q3 budget conversation?

elements.name: Competition
elements.evidence: Status quo is contracted inspection crews
elements.missing: Other drone vendors being evaluated or in-house drone programs
elements.discovery_question: Are you looking at any other drone or automation options alongside FlytBase?

industry_fit.reason: Lithium extraction in the Atacama Desert: heavy mining with large outdoor assets

pain_severity.reason: "Contracted crews are expensive and hazardous" - cost and safety pain autonomy removes, but not quantified

buyer_authority.reason: "Head of Operations, Northern Operations Division" - senior operational owner, budget authority not confirmed

timing_and_budget.reason: "Internal budget conversation scheduled for Q3" - budget process exists but no amount or committed timeline

risks: Budget not yet approved; depends on Q3 internal conversation
Economic buyer and procurement path unknown
Harsh desert conditions (heat, dust, connectivity) may raise technical requirements
Large mining procurement may require tenders and local partner involvement
Incumbent contracted crew providers are the status quo
summary: SQM is a strong ICP fit: a major lithium miner with 3 large 24/7 Atacama sites, clear cost and safety pain, a senior operations contact and a warm referral from Anglo American. Priority is high, held back only by the unconfirmed economic buyer, decision and paper process, with budget pending a Q3 conversation.
